With a browser-network fixture answering 413 for the Version upload, Add version stayed open with "DOC-030 fixture: this file is larger than the upload limit.". The chain still had 4 Versions with identical ids, numbers, types, notes and pin. The attachment offered File to Contract. File attachment opened with Destination "New Document" (options New Document / New Version on an existing Document), the switch "Confidential — restrict to the contract team" already on, and Type starting on "No type" with the Contract list. File created "DOC-030 Admin filed paper 09251116" (Confidential, one Version, Type Draft · theirs) and the comment read "Filed to DOC-030 Admin filed paper 09251116, version 1". Selecting the attachment name opened its preview with File to Contract. New Version on an existing Document, Document "DOC-030 Admin supply draft 09251116" and a Note appended v5 with that note; the comment read "Filed to DOC-030 Admin supply draft 09251116, version 5". The Matter attachment offered File to Matter. File attachment showed Type starting on "No type" with No type, DOC-030 documents Matter type 09251116, and the switch "Confidential — restrict to the matter team". File created "DOC-030 Admin matter filed 09251116" typed "DOC-030 documents Matter type 09251116". Amara Nwosu (Business User, on the C-331 team) opened /portal/contracts/331: the Documents section listed "DOC-030 Admin supply draft 09251116" with no select and no "Type of version" control. limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and technical reviewer; not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.

work2 is shared with other DOC-030 agents. Only records named DOC-030 documents were created. The two Document types this run added were archived at its end; archive keeps their labels on the Versions that carry them. Types other agents added appeared in the Contract and Matter pickers and are not credited.

The Generated redline check used a Word Comparison of v1 to v2 requested and exported through the lab API as fixture setup; the browser checked the resulting Type cell. The guide's Comparison export steps belong to compare-versions.md.
A Version generated by an Auto-Doc was not exercised: the seed has no Auto-Doc generations. Source (documents-card.tsx TypeCell readOnly for source generated; routes.ts 409) shows it is read-only.

The failed upload used a controlled 413 browser response; the lab's real upload limit was not reached. The refused type corrections (archived record, Generated redline, Knowledge Item, Business User) are real server answers.
Insufficient access used Amara Nwosu, a seeded Business User on the Contract team, in the Portal. The lab has no Contributor account, so the Contributor refusal the API documents was not exercised.

Confirmed the author's product bug: on a Knowledge Item the Type column renders a select (No type plus the item's Knowledge type) and every choice is refused. Choosing No type shows "That version already has this type."; the Knowledge type id sent directly answers 400 "Pick a document type from this record's list." The guide describes this behavior, so it is not a guide failure.
The Portal still labels its Contract upload control Kind (author limitation); this guide does not describe Portal controls and it was not checked.
The Entity empty-list check ran only in the Administrator pass, before the run added its Entity type; the Legal pass ran after it, so it saw a non-empty Entity list.
